facts.fact: EuroMedAI says Organic Law No. 53.25, promulgated by Dahir No. 1.25.70 on 16 January 2026, names AI tools among the means of electoral offences, including a new Article 51 bis on fabricated content, with penalties of 2 to 5 years and MAD 50,000-100,000.

EuroMedAI says HACA Decision No. 50-26 of 16 June 2026 prohibits broadcasting falsified or AI-generated electoral content liable to mislead the public and requires a notice on AI-generated educational content on radio and television.

EuroMedAI says HACA, the audiovisual authority, adopted Decision No. 50-26 on AI-generated electoral content on radio and television, and the CNDP issued guidance in late August 2026 asking that AI-produced content be identified.

MAR.note: No government body's use of AI is stated.

facts.fact: EuroMedAI says Organic Law No. 53.25, promulgated on 16 January 2026, names artificial intelligence tools among the means by which electoral offences can be committed.
EuroMedAI says the electoral provisions are not part of a general law on AI.

MAR.note: No AI tool in a public sector system is stated.
No AI model, dataset or computing built in Morocco is stated.
No identity authentication service is described.
No link between birth registration and ID is described.

facts.fact: EuroMedAI says the CNDP issued guidance at the end of August 2026 to political parties on processing voters' data under Law No. 09-08.
EuroMedAI says the CNDP, the National Commission for the Control of Personal Data Protection, issued guidance under Law No. 09-08 and opened a helpline, 3020.
EuroMedAI says the CNDP's guidance to parties recalls duties to declare processing, obtain consent and control transfers abroad, and asks that AI-produced content be identified.

MAR.note: Accessible AI campaign content is an observation topic only; no ID or service access is stated.
No national ID coverage is described.
No ID issuance from birth is described.
No ID register upkeep is described.
Digital identity is named only as a topic of the Digital X.0 draft.

facts.fact: EuroMedAI says a draft framework law known as Digital X.0, covering data governance, digital identity and interoperability, was reported in late 2025 to be under review at the General Secretariat of the Government.

EuroMedAI says opposition members in the House of Representatives proposed deleting part of Article 51 bis of Organic Law 53.25, arguing it could restrict freedom of expression; the Government did not accept the amendment.
